strengths: The paper introduces a novel and theoretically grounded metric (empowerment) for evaluating text-based LM agents without relying on handcrafted goals or reward functions.

The proposed EELMA algorithm effectively handles natural language variability and high-dimensional observations by projecting text to compact embedding spaces and training dual InfoNCE-based neural estimators.
The evaluation is thorough, spanning both simple controlled textual games (Gridworld, Tower of Hanoi) with analytical ground truths and complex real-world benchmarks (WebArena, τ-bench).

The paper provides valuable insights into how different agent designs (e.g., Chain-of-Thought, memory context length, model size) impact empowerment, demonstrating a strong correlation with task performance.
The analysis of 'pivotal moments' (such as authentication/login events) shows the practical utility of the metric for safety and behavior monitoring.
weaknesses: The empowerment metric has notable boundary conditions (which the authors carefully document), such as failing when reasoning is the performance bottleneck, when agents exert task-irrelevant control (e.g., navigating off-domain), or when all models operate near floor performance.
Due to the InfoNCE approximation, the estimated empowerment can sometimes take negative values, which limits the physical interpretability of the absolute values of the metric.
The estimation requires training an embedding encoder and collecting a large number of trajectories, which introduces extra computational overhead compared to direct evaluation metrics.
For some of the experiments, particularly the τ-bench evaluations, the sample size of models is very small (only 3 Qwen models), making some of the correlation claims less statistically robust.

strengths: Compelling and highly original concept of using empowerment, an information-theoretic measure, as a goal-agnostic evaluation metric for language model agents.

Well-designed and robust methodology (EELMA) that successfully overcomes the high-dimensionality and linguistic redundancy of text environments by leveraging InfoNCE and pretrained embeddings with LoRA.

Rigorous empirical validation: the paper compares EELMA against ground-truth analytical empowerment in toy domains (Gridworld, Tower of Hanoi) and shows excellent estimation accuracy ($R_s = 0.80 - 0.94$).

Extensive testing across realistic, complex environments like WebArena and $\tau$-bench with various model scales (from 1.5B to closed-source frontier models), showing strong correlation with mean discounted rewards.
An insightful case study on authentication/power-seeking behaviors, highlighting how the metric can organically detect pivotal transitions without hand-labeled milestones.
Very transparent discussion of failure modes and boundaries (e.g., when reasoning is the bottleneck, or when floor-performance hallucination inflates estimated empowerment).
weaknesses: EELMA requires collecting a substantial number of trajectories (e.g., several hundred to over a thousand) to ensure the contrastive estimation converges, which can be computationally and financially expensive for frontier API-based agents.
Sensitivity to embedding quality: as analyzed in the appendix, the accuracy of EELMA is highly dependent on the choice of the base text encoder and training hyperparameters.

The 'hallucinated empowerment' failure mode in the retail domain (where a weaker model's invalid/erratic actions lead to high estimated MI) remains a critical limitation for evaluating low-performing or unaligned models, as it complicates the interpretation of the metric.

strengths: Proposes a novel and interesting direction by applying information-theoretic empowerment to evaluate language model agents, which is a promising alternative to goal-centric benchmarks.
Provides a thorough empirical evaluation across a wide spectrum of environments, from structured toy tasks (Gridworld, Tower of Hanoi) to complex agent benchmarks (WebArena, τ-bench).
Presents extensive ablation studies exploring the impacts of base encoders, fine-tuning techniques (LoRA vs. frozen), and agent architectures (Chain-of-Thought, memory context).
Honestly documents the limitations, failure modes, and boundary conditions of empowerment estimation in the discussion.
weaknesses: Mathematical Unsoundness of the Estimator: In Section 3 (Equation 6) and Appendix G.4, the EELMA estimator is computed by subtracting two separately trained InfoNCE critics. This subtraction is theoretically unsound. The InfoNCE objective is invariant to adding any arbitrary function of the conditioning variable, i.e., $f(x, y) \to f(x, y) + c(x)$ yields the exact same loss because $c(x)$ cancels out in the denominator. Thus, the learned critics contain unconstrained, arbitrary functions $C_1(o_t, a_t)$ and $C_2(o_t)$ that do not necessarily cancel out or vanish as negative-sample size $K \to \infty$. This unconstrained shift explains why the estimator frequently yields negative empowerment values (Figure 9 and Appendix G.4), which is mathematically impossible for true mutual information.

Vulnerability to Metric Inversion and Gaming: The empirical results demonstrate that EELMA is highly sensitive to non-purposeful behavioral diversity. In \u03c4-bench retail, weaker models receive higher empowerment scores because they hallucinate invalid tool calls and trigger diverse error messages. Similarly, in WebArena Reddit, jailbreaking behavior (navigating off-domain) artificially inflates empowerment scores. A reliable agent evaluation metric should not reward chaotic failures, hallucinations, or safety violations with higher capability ratings.

Limited Scope of Empowerment as a Proxy: The core hypothesis that empowerment correlates with general agentic capability fails in environments where the primary bottleneck is reasoning or mathematical correctness rather than state reachability (e.g., WebArena Shopping). This limits the applicability of the metric to navigation-heavy tasks.
Incomplete Text: The manuscript contains multiple unfinished placeholder sentences, such as 'Code available: ' on Page 1 and 'The EELMA code is available at ' on Page 18.

strengths: Highly original and timely concept: Porting the information-theoretic RL concept of 'empowerment' (an agent's capacity to influence its future states) to the evaluation and safety monitoring of natural language LLM agents.

Sound and robust methodology: The proposed EELMA algorithm effectively utilizes contrastive successor representations combined with text embeddings to successfully handle the high dimensionality, sparsity, and linguistic variability of text-based environments.

Rigorous empirical validation: The framework is comprehensively tested on structured environments (Gridworld, Tower of Hanoi) where ground-truth direct estimation is possible, as well as on a scaled-up, realistic web-browsing task (WebArena).

Excellent robustness to natural language variability: The authors demonstrate that EELMA maintains accurate estimates even when state descriptions are paraphrased, showing a clear advantage over direct statistical baselines that fail under linguistic diversity.

Insightful case study on safety: The authentication case study elegantly demonstrates how empowerment can highlight pivotal, highly influential actions (such as gaining admin access via manual login) in a completely unsupervised, goal-agnostic manner.
weaknesses: High computational and sample cost: Estimating empowerment via EELMA requires collecting thousands of multi-turn trajectories and training a contrastive neural network. The high cost of API calls to collect these trajectories for frontier LLMs may limit its feasibility as a standard quick evaluation tool.

Strong theoretical assumptions: The theoretical foundation linking empowerment to performance relies on strong idealizations (e.g., the uniform reward goals assumption and Boltzmann rationality) which do not fully reflect realistic web tasks where goals are highly sparse and concentrated.

Decoupling in highly cognitive tasks: As shown in the WebArena 'Shopping' domain, empowerment can decouple from actual task success if the task bottleneck lies in precise cognitive or logical reasoning (e.g., numerical price comparison) rather than environmental optionality.

strengths: Novel application of information-theoretic empowerment to language model agents, offering a promising, goal-agnostic evaluation paradigm.
Methodological soundness: EELMA successfully bridges text-based environments and variational mutual information estimation by learning robust, low-dimensional representations.

Strong empirical validation: The paper evaluates the method on controlled environments (Gridworld, Tower of Hanoi) to compare against exact ground-truth calculations, as well as on a complex, real-world benchmark (WebArena).
Insightful safety and monitoring analysis: The power-seeking and authentication case study showcases how EELMA can detect pivotal transitions (such as successful login) without hand-labeled rewards.
Robustness to language variation: Demonstrates that EELMA handles semantic variations of the same underlying state much better than direct count-based estimation or prompt-only LLM-based estimation.
weaknesses: Computational and sample complexity: Estimating empowerment requires collecting a large number of multi-turn trajectories and training contrastive neural encoders, which is computationally expensive and costly, particularly for large API-based models.

Limitations in environments with reasoning bottlenecks: As seen in the WebArena Shopping domain, empowerment does not correlate well with task performance when specific mathematical or reasoning skills act as a bottleneck rather than environmental control.

Minor mathematical ambiguities in Section 3: The formulation in Equation (1) is a bit mathematically loose, as the expectation is written outside of the sum over $t$, but the future state random variable $s^*$ (which depends on $t$ and $	au$) is used inside the log-ratio within the sum, making the scope of the random variables slightly confusing.

strengths: Presents a novel and compelling application of the cybernetic/RL concept of empowerment to Language Model (LM) agents, offering a path toward goal-agnostic capability evaluation.
Validates the proposed EELMA framework across both synthetic environments (Gridworld, Tower of Hanoi) and a highly realistic, complex web-navigation benchmark (WebArena).

Provides thorough ablation studies examining how various LLM agent components (such as Chain-of-Thought, memory length, model scale, and open vs. closed architectures) influence the estimated empowerment.
Demonstrates excellent robustness to linguistic variability (synonyms and rephrasings), where standard direct-estimation baselines fail due to vocabulary mismatches.
weaknesses: Mathematical notation and typos: In Equation 1, the conditioning in the mutual information term is written as $I(a_t; s^* | a)$ instead of $I(a_t; s^* | s_t)$. Additionally, the notation combining the trajectory expectation with the discounted infinite sum is somewhat convoluted, as $s^*$ is already defined as a discounted future state.

Dependence on goal-directed trajectories: While empowerment is technically goal-agnostic, evaluating LM agents still requires prompting them with goals to generate meaningful actions. Without goals, LLM agents often degenerate into repetitive or incoherent outputs, meaning the evaluation process is still implicitly tied to a distribution of task prompts.

Incremental algorithmic novelty: The core variational mutual information estimation via successor representations relies heavily on the formulation introduced by Myers et al. (2025). The primary contribution here is the extension to language spaces via embedding models.

High computational and environment-specific overhead: EELMA requires collecting large sets of trajectories and training neural encoders ($\phi$ and $\psi$) for several hours on a GPU for each environment. This reduces its utility as a quick, plug-and-play evaluation metric compared to conventional benchmarks.

Visual presentation in Figure 7: The domain-wise correlation plots in Figure 7(B) are extremely compressed, with overlapping text that makes them difficult to read. Furthermore, the weak/slightly negative correlation ($r = -0.11$) in the Shopping domain is a notable limitation that warrants a deeper discussion on when empowerment fails to track performance.
